nodes.content: Develop a learned plasma fluid closure that recovers collisionless plasma echoes while preserving energy under unseen forcing histories.
requirements: Predict echo amplitudes within 10% of Vlasov–Poisson reference values on held-out forcing histories.
Keep unforced total energy drift below 0.1% over 100 plasma periods.

nodes.content: Train a skew-symmetric Hamiltonian fluid closure with Fourier–Hermite memory modes for echo recovery and exact unforced energy conservation.
How many Hermite memory modes preserve echo amplitudes within 10% across unseen two-pulse delays of 10–40 plasma periods?
At kλ_D=0.1, 256 Hermite modes achieve ≤10% echo-amplitude error for held-out 10–40-plasma-period delays; 32 modes do not.
Train 32/64/128/256-mode closures at kλ_D=0.1; compare echo errors across held-out 10–40-period delays and unforced 100-period energy drift.
Run VP-Echo40: train four Hermite-mode closures at kλ_D=0.1; measure held-out echo errors and 100-period unforced energy drift.
VP-Echo40 report with four trained closure checkpoints, held-out echo-amplitude errors, and 100-period unforced energy-drift traces.
Audit VP-Echo40 report using its checkpoints and traces; recompute per-delay echo errors and energy drift to test 256-versus-32-mode hypothesis.
VP-Echo40 audit found 14% echo-amplitude error for 256 modes at 40 periods, exceeding 10%; 32-mode error was 31%.
At kλ_D=0.1, 512 Hermite modes achieve ≤10% echo-amplitude error across held-out 10–40-period delays; 256 modes fail at 40 periods.
Initialize and train a 512-mode closure from VP-Echo40's 256-mode checkpoint; test held-out 10–40-period echoes and 100-period energy drift.
VP-Echo40’s 512-mode closure achieved 8.2% maximum held-out echo-amplitude error across 10–40-period delays; unforced 100-period energy drift was 0.03%.
Re-run VP-Echo40’s 256-mode checkpoint against the 512-mode closure on new 10–40-period forcing histories, measuring maximum echo error.
New forcing histories yielded 12.6% echo error for 512 modes versus 16.4% for 256 modes at 35 periods.
Is the 512-mode error on new 35-period forcing histories due to limited training-history coverage rather than Hermite truncation?
Across 10–40-period histories, phase/amplitude-augmented 512-mode training yields ≤10% echo error; unaugmented 1024 modes exceed 10% at 35 periods.
Extend VP-Echo40’s 256-mode checkpoint into phase/amplitude-augmented 512 and unaugmented 1024 modes; compare against unaugmented 512 on unseen 10–40-period echoes.
On matched-distribution histories, unaugmented 512 modes achieved 9.1% maximum error across 10–40-period delays; 256 modes reached 14% at 40.
On shifted-phase 35-period histories, augmented 512 modes had 11.2% echo error; unaugmented 1024 modes had 8.4%.
Using VP-Echo40 checkpoints, train matched augmented and unaugmented 512- and 1024-mode closures; compare shifted-phase 10–40-period echo errors and energy drift.
On new phase/amplitude-shifted histories, augmented 512 modes had 9.3% maximum echo error; unaugmented 1024 reached 11.0% at 35 periods.
Defer architecture selection: 512 modes pass matched histories, but shifted-phase tests reverse the augmented-512 versus unaugmented-1024 ranking.
Train a Hamiltonian recurrent closure with adaptive phase-mixing memory and worst-case echo loss across forcing-phase shifts.
Does adaptive memory reduce worst-case shifted-phase echo error below 10% while keeping 100-period unforced energy drift below 0.1%?
A 128-state symplectic recurrent memory yields ≤9% worst-case shifted-phase echo error and ≤0.05% unforced energy drift over 100 periods.
Train a 128-state symplectic recurrent closure on VP-Echo40; measure worst-case shifted-phase echo error and 100-period unforced energy drift.
The 128-state closure achieved 7.8% worst-case shifted-phase echo error, but unforced energy drift reached 0.13% over 100 periods.
Discrete-gradient stepping of the 128-state closure retains ≤9% worst-case shifted-phase echo error and lowers 100-period energy drift below 0.05%.
Replace symplectic stepping with discrete-gradient updates in the trained 128-state closure; rerun shifted-phase echoes and 100-period unforced energy tests.
Discrete-gradient stepping lowered 100-period unforced energy drift to 0.012%, but worst-case shifted-phase echo error rose to 11.4%.
Retrain the 128-state closure end-to-end with discrete-gradient stepping and worst-case shifted-phase echo loss; retest echo error and energy drift.
End-to-end discrete-gradient retraining yielded 8.6% worst-case shifted-phase echo error and 0.018% unforced energy drift over 100 periods.
Does the discrete-gradient closure retain sub-10% echo error on held-out three-pulse histories without exceeding 0.1% unforced energy drift?
Mixed-pulse training gives the 128-state discrete-gradient closure ≤10% worst-case held-out three-pulse echo error and ≤0.05% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Train mixed-pulse 128-state discrete-gradient closure; compare against two-pulse-trained baseline on shifted-phase two-/three-pulse echo errors and 100-period energy drift.
The two-pulse-trained discrete-gradient baseline retained 8.6% worst-case shifted-phase two-pulse echo error and 0.018% 100-period energy drift.
Mixed-pulse training yielded 13.1% worst-case held-out three-pulse echo error; 100-period unforced energy drift was 0.021%.
Fine-tune the 13.1%-error mixed-pulse closure with additional uniformly sampled three-pulse histories; retest held-out echo error and 100-period energy drift.
After three-pulse fine-tuning, the mixed-pulse closure achieved 9.4% worst-case held-out echo error and 0.023% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Select the fine-tuned discrete-gradient closure: 9.4% three-pulse error and 0.023% 100-period drift resolve regressions beyond the two-pulse baseline.
Learn a Mori–Zwanzig memory kernel using conservative auxiliary oscillators to retain echo phase information without energy leakage.
How many conservative auxiliary oscillators keep unseen 10–40-period echo error below 10% and unforced 100-period energy drift below 0.1%?
At kλ_D=0.1, 64 oscillators achieve ≤10% held-out echo error across 10–40-period delays and ≤0.05% 100-period unforced energy drift.
Fit 16/32/64/128-oscillator kernels at kλ_D=0.1; compare unseen two-pulse echo errors and unforced 100-period energy drift against Vlasov–Poisson.
Run MZ-Echo40: train four oscillator-count kernels at kλ_D=0.1 and evaluate held-out echo amplitudes and 100-period unforced energy.
MZ-Echo40 benchmark bundle containing four oscillator-kernel checkpoints, held-out echo amplitudes, and 100-period unforced energy traces.
Audit MZ-Echo40 checkpoints against Vlasov–Poisson, recomputing 64-oscillator held-out echo errors and 100-period unforced energy drift.
MZ-Echo40’s 64-oscillator kernel achieved 8.7% maximum held-out two-pulse echo error and 0.016% unforced energy drift over 100 periods.
Advance the 64-oscillator kernel to broader forcing tests: its 8.7% two-pulse echo error and 0.016% energy drift meet thresholds.
Train a Hamiltonian multi-stream fluid closure with learned velocity nodes and discrete-gradient integration to preserve echo phases and energy.
How many learned velocity streams recover held-out 10–40-period echo amplitudes within 10% while maintaining sub-0.1% unforced energy drift?
At kλ_D=0.1, 48 learned streams achieve ≤10% worst-case held-out echo error and ≤0.05% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Train 24/48/96-stream discrete-gradient closures on VP-Echo40; benchmark held-out 10–40-period echo errors and 100-period unforced energy drift.
The 48-stream closure reached 12.2% worst-case held-out echo error; unforced 100-period energy drift was 0.009%.
At kλ_D=0.1, 96 learned streams reduce worst-case held-out echo error below 10%, with unforced 100-period energy drift below 0.05%.
Rebenchmark 48- and 96-stream checkpoints on new held-out 10–40-period forcing histories; measure worst-case echo error and 100-period energy drift.
On new matched-distribution histories, 48 streams achieved 9.6% worst-case echo error and 0.010% unforced 100-period energy drift.
On shifted-phase 40-period histories, 96 streams incurred 11.1% worst-case echo error despite 0.012% unforced energy drift.
Reconcile 48-stream 12.2% versus 9.6% echo errors by stratifying forcing phases; retest worst-case error and 100-period energy drift.
Phase-stratified audit traced 12.2% to misaligned reference peaks; corrected 48-stream worst-case error was 9.8%, with 0.010% energy drift.
Advance 48 streams for matched-distribution tests after peak-alignment correction; defer broad deployment because 96 streams fail shifted-phase echoes.
Fit a phase-equivariant nonlinear Volterra closure with antisymmetric energy-transfer channels and adaptive delay kernels for multi-pulse forcing.
Does phase equivariance keep three-pulse echo error below 10% across unseen phases and delays while limiting 100-period energy drift?
A 32-lag phase-equivariant Volterra closure achieves ≤9% worst-case held-out three-pulse echo error and ≤0.05% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Train 16/32/64-lag Volterra closures on VP-Echo40 two-/three-pulse histories; test shifted-phase echo error and 100-period unforced energy drift.
Run Volterra-Echo40: fit 16/32/64-lag phase-equivariant kernels and score held-out three-pulse echo amplitudes and unforced energy traces.
Volterra-Echo40 bundle with 16/32/64-lag checkpoints, shifted-phase three-pulse echo scores, and 100-period unforced energy traces.
Audit Volterra-Echo40’s 32-lag checkpoint and the 48-stream closure against Vlasov–Poisson on shifted-phase echoes and 100-period unforced energy drift.
Volterra-Echo40’s 32-lag closure achieved 8.8% worst-case shifted-phase three-pulse echo error and 0.031% unforced 100-period energy drift.
The 48-stream comparator yielded 9.7% worst-case held-out two-pulse echo error and 0.010% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Prioritize the 32-lag Volterra closure for three-pulse tests; retain 48 streams as the lower-drift two-pulse comparator.
Prioritize 32-lag Volterra for broader validation (8.8% three-pulse error, 0.031% drift); retain recurrent, oscillator, stream, and Hermite comparators.
